sentences.text: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Sindhu Sharma, Judge

Order 
01. The Civil First Miscellaneous Appeal is directed against the judgment and award dated 27.11.2008 passed by the learned District Judge, Ramban whereby the reference made under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act for enhancement of the compensation has been rejected.

02. Acquisition proceedings of land measuring 03 Kanals 13 Marlas in survey No. 810 situated in village Batote, Tehsil and District Ramban for construction of the office building of Deputy Inspector General Police Udhampur Range, Hqrs Batote, was initiated on the requisition of Deputy Inspector General of Police, Doda/Udhampur Range vide his communication dated 16.04.1996.
03. Final award was passed on 06.04.1999 by the Collector Land Acquisition (Additional Deputy Commissioner), Ramban awarding compensation of Rs. 2,72,837.50 to the petitioner.

04. Aggrieved of the award of the Collector Land Acquisition, the petitioner sought a reference under Section 18 of the J&K Land Acquisition Act claiming fair and equitable compensation for the acquired land.

This reference was dismissed by the Additional District Judge, Ramban vide judgment dated 16.05.2002.
05.
An appeal against the dismissal of the reference vide judgment dated 16.05.2022 was filed by the petitioner before this Court.

This appeal i.e., CIMA No. 144/2002 was allowed and the judgment dated 16.05.2002 was set aside, the case was remanded for deciding it afresh in accordance with Salima vs Collector Land Acquisition And on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61962752/
1 law.

06. The District Judge, Ramban, while deciding the reference afresh, rejected the same vide judgment dated 27.11.2008.
07.

The present appeal has been preferred by the petitioner against the impugned judgment dated 27.11.2008 on the ground that the compensation awarded by the Collector is inadequate and the same be enhanced.
It is also specifically averred that despite an award having been passed, the possession of the land has neither been taken by the Collector nor by the Department.

08. Perusal of the record reveals that the office of Deputy Commissioner, Ramban on the request of the Collector Land Acquisition, Ramban vide his communication No.ACQ/Gen/01-03 dated 02.04.2012 has reported and recommended that the Indenting Department DIG (Police)
Doda-Kishtwar-Ramban Range headquarters Batote, has made a request to withdraw the acquisition proceedings of the aforesaid case and accordingly, the land measuring 03 Kanals 13 Marlas in survey No. 810 situated in village Batote (MC Limits) was de-notified vide order No.
DC/Rbm/LA/03- 09 dated 04.04.2012.
09.

After de-notification of the land, the Intending Department has moved an application before the District Judge, Ramban for release of FDR amounting to Rs.2,72,838/- to Miscellaneous Police Revenue Account Head 0055 which was allowed and FDR along with interest was released in favour of the Miscellaneous Police Revenue Account.
10. Thus, the only issue to be considered is whether after the passing of award, the respondents could withdraw from the acquisition and de-notify the land.
Rule 43 of J&K Land Acquisition Rules provides for opportunity to withdraw from the Acquisition on certain conditions.

It reads as under:-
"43. Opportunity of withdrawal to be given to acquiring department.
A second and equally important point is that in certain cases the department for which the land is being acquired will be allowed an opportunity of withdrawing from the transaction.

It is imperative that such opportunity should be given before possession has actually been taken and it is to be observed that this permits withdrawal even after the award has been announced and compensation paid; provided only the possession has not passed.
Once possession has passed, the Collector's award becomes binding on Government who has no power to claim a reference to the Court under Section 18 of the Act.
It follows that Government's power of withdrawal must be exercised at some stage of the proceedings.
Such stages would be:-
11. Rule-43 of the Rules provides for withdrawal from acquisition in certain cases
, even after the award has been announced and compensation paid, the only condition is that the possession has not passed.
The award has been passed on 06.04.1999, the physical possession of the land is admittedly with the petitioner and possession has not been held.
In fact, the respondents have de-notified the Salima vs Collector Land Acquisition And on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61962752/
2 land and even taken the amount deposited with the trial Court
. The only person, who could raise a grievance against the de- notification and challenge the same but they are not aggrieved of the same.

The respondents in terms of Rule-43 could withdraw from the acquisition proceedings even after the award has been pronounced as the possession had not passed, as the physical possession of the land is with the petitioner till date.

12. In view of the admitted facts and circumstances, this appeal has become infructuous and is,
accordingly, disposed of.
(Sindhu Sharma) Judge JAMMU 09.05.2023
